rationale: Spring Boot v4.0.7 pins springFrameworkVersion=7.0.8. A request for '/' is handled by spring-boot's autoconfigured WelcomePageHandlerMapping, whose getAcceptedMediaTypes() reads the request Accept header and calls MediaType.parseMediaTypes(acceptHeader), catching only the checked InvalidMediaTypeException. MediaType.parseMediaType delegates to spring-core's MimeTypeUtils.parseMimeType -> parseMimeTypeInternal, which scans the string and, on a double-quote, tests `mimeType.charAt(nextIndex - 1) != '\\'` to see if the quote is escaped. For a value that begins with a quote (e.g. `"text/html"` with no ';' section) the scan reaches the quote at nextIndex == 0 and reads charAt(-1), throwing an unchecked java.lang.StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. That is not the checked InvalidMediaTypeException the welcome-page handler catches, so it escapes as a 500. This is a regression introduced by spring-framework commit 41cd6879bd (quoted-pair parsing) and present at tag v7.0.8. The real upstream fix (commit 4d6e88dc988e, after v7.0.8) guards the index: `(nextIndex == 0 || mimeType.charAt(nextIndex - 1) != '\\')`, so a leading quote is handled without the out-of-bounds read and the value fails as a normal invalid media type. The spring-web and spring-boot files are the traversal that leads an investigator across the module and repo boundary.

required_files.rationale: Fix site: parseMimeTypeInternal scans for quotes and does `mimeType.charAt(nextIndex - 1) != '\\'`; for a value starting with a quote, nextIndex == 0 makes charAt(-1) throw an unchecked StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of the checked InvalidMimeTypeException. Real upstream fix (commit 4d6e88dc988e) guards with `nextIndex == 0 ||`.

Hop: parseMediaTypes -> parseMediaType delegates to MimeTypeUtils.parseMimeType and re-wraps InvalidMimeTypeException as InvalidMediaTypeException; the bridge from the Accept-header parse into the core mime-type text parser where the index goes out of bounds.

Entry/boundary: the autoconfigured handler for '/' reads the request Accept header in getAcceptedMediaTypes() and calls MediaType.parseMediaTypes(...), catching only the checked InvalidMediaTypeException, so an unchecked index error from the core parser escapes as a 500.
